How do atmospheric acid input, accessible neutralisation, reference alkalinity, and water export combine in an annual budget?

Use with the [integrated case](../integrated-case/notes.qmd) and its [exercises](../integrated-case/exercise.qmd). This working week revisits earlier reactions in a connected chemical explanation.

## Predict first

Predict how halving the water-equivalent alkalinity concentration differs from halving the annual alkalinity export. Which input changes can cause each?

## Questions to try

1. Choose **Worked catchment**. Close the acid budget in annual equivalents before looking at concentrations.
2. Choose **Less neutralisation**. Trace the effect on residual acidity and reference-adjusted alkalinity.
3. Choose **Double water export**. Verify that annual acid and alkalinity amounts stay fixed while their flow-weighted concentrations halve.
4. Choose **Capacity exceeds input**. Why is unused capacity not counted as newly generated alkalinity in this comparison?
5. Choose **Exceed reference alkalinity**. Explain the signed negative alkalinity result without calling it a negative concentration or inferring a pH.

## Hand check and static reference

| Quantity | Worked catchment | Less neutralisation |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Acid input | 40000 eq/year | 40000 eq/year |
| Acid actually neutralised | 30000 eq/year | 20000 eq/year |
| Residual acid | 10000 eq/year | 20000 eq/year |
| Reference alkalinity export | 50000 eq/year | 50000 eq/year |
| Adjusted alkalinity export | 40000 eq/year | 30000 eq/year |
| Adjusted alkalinity, at 500 million L/year | 0.0800 meq/L | 0.0600 meq/L |

The base residual acidity is **0.0200 meq/L**. It differs from the week 1
before-neutralisation value because this budget includes acid consumed in the
catchment.

## Model conditions

This is a constructed **annual** equivalent budget, not a dynamic lake model. Accessible capacity caps how much of the added acid can react; unused capacity is not credited as extra alkalinity. Residual acidity is subtracted from an explicitly supplied reference annual alkalinity export. The other terms stay fixed when one slider changes. A real change in water flow could also alter weathering, transport, and retention. A pH prediction requires inorganic carbon, gas exchange, and appropriate acid–base constraints. Use the [closed-water demo](week2.qmd) for the separate pulse problem.

What additional measurements would you need to connect this annual budget to a lake’s pH response and test whether neutralisation really changed?
